task_instance: Audit and clean up the source-code comments in a small representative TypeScript module (a user-service file) that mixes low-value and high-value commentary, applying the lean-comments necessity test, decision order, and style rules, while leaving executable code and behavior unchanged.
evidence: Skill is a pure comment-policy/judgment skill with no bundled scripts (only SKILL.md present next to it); it needs only text read/write, which the offline runtime provides. Created input sample userService.before.ts (22 comment-like lines) exercising every target category: a file-header export-summary, a label comment on an interface, what-narration comments, an obvious guard/return comment, a trailing redundant comment, a useless JSDoc that only restates the signature, a genuine positional-constraint rationale, an eslint suppression directive, a bare Never-warning plus a supported credential-redaction rationale, a completed/stale TODO, and commented-out dead code. Produced userService.after.ts by applying the decision order: deleted all label/narration/obvious comments and the type-restating JSDoc; converted the caller-visible private-profile behavior into concise declaration documentation (per the skill's high-value example); kept the source-order positional-constraint comment and the credential-redaction rationale (supported, non-obvious); kept the eslint suppression directive intact; removed the stale completed TODO and the commented-out code. Verification: comment-like lines dropped from 22 to 6; grep confirmed the 6 retained items are exactly the two justified rationale comments, the preserved tooling directive, and the rewritten 3-line JSDoc. A node-based strip of ALL comment forms showed executable code is byte-identical before vs after (printed 'executable code identical: true'), confirming no behavior/statement change; braces, parens, and JSDoc blocks are balanced/closed. Files: userService.before.ts, userService.after.ts, result.json in the work directory.
